sources.entry: Usertour - User onboarding platform allowing you to create in-app product tours, checklists, and surveys in minutes effortlessly. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Usertour is an open-source, self-hostable user onboarding platform for building in-app product tours, checklists, launchers, and surveys.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Usertour as an open-source user onboarding platform for creating in-app product tours, checklists, launchers, and surveys. It says it works in any browser-based app, including single-page and multi-page apps, and supports custom user attributes and event tracking for targeting. Flows can be organized across environments such as Production and Staging, with version tracking of changes. Appearance (text, button colors, font family, size) can be customized with multiple themes. The README also mentions analytics on views, completion rates, and drop-off points per step. It includes a built-in MCP server so AI assistants can generate onboarding flows in a project. Self-hosting is done with Docker Compose.
use_cases: build in-app product tours for a web app
run product feedback surveys inside an app
track where users drop off in onboarding flows
self-host an alternative to Appcues or Userpilot
segment users for targeted in-app messages
how_to_run: cp .env.example .env # make sure all required envs are properly set
notable: Open-source alternative to commercial onboarding tools such as Appcues, Userpilot, Userflow, Userguiding, and Chameleon
Built-in MCP server lets AI assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex generate onboarding flows in your project
Multiple environments (e.g. Production and Staging) and version tracking within one account
Community edition is MIT-licensed; enterprise code for paid self-hosted plans has a separate license
caveats: Enterprise self-hosted Business and Enterprise plans are governed by a separate enterprise license and require contacting the company for private deployment
Self-hosting setup requires configuring environment variables; detailed instructions are in external documentation
summary.license: AGPL-3.0 (per listing metadata); README states community code is MIT and enterprise code is under LICENSE.enterprise
keywords: walk new users through my app
